legend: This is a harder version of the problem. In this version, n≤50000%%ZSMJ0%%.

There are n%%ZSMJ1%% distinct points in three-dimensional space numbered from 1%%ZSMJ2%% to n%%ZSMJ3%%. The i%%ZSMJ4%%-th point has coordinates (xi,yi,zi)%%ZSMJ5%%. The number of points n%%ZSMJ6%% is even.

You'd like to remove all n%%ZSMJ7%% points using a sequence of n2%%ZSMJ8%% snaps. In one snap, you can remove any two points a%%ZSMJ9%% and b%%ZSMJ10%% that have not been removed yet and form a perfectly balanced pair. A pair of points a%%ZSMJ11%% and b%%ZSMJ12%% is perfectly balanced if no other point c%%ZSMJ13%% (that has not been removed yet) lies within the axis-aligned minimum bounding box of points a%%ZSMJ14%% and b%%ZSMJ15%%.

Formally, point c%%ZSMJ16%% lies within the axis-aligned minimum bounding box of points a%%ZSMJ17%% and b%%ZSMJ18%% if and only if min%%ZSMJ19%%, \min(y_a, y_b) \le y_c \le \max(y_a, y_b)%%ZSMJ20%%, and \min(z_a, z_b) \le z_c \le \max(z_a, z_b)%%ZSMJ21%%. Note that the bounding box might be degenerate.
Find a way to remove all points in \frac{n}{2}%%ZSMJ22%% snaps.
input: The first line contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ23%% (2 \le n \le 50\,000%%ZSMJ24%%; n%%ZSMJ25%% is even), denoting the number of points.

Each of the next n%%ZSMJ26%% lines contains three integers x_i%%ZSMJ27%%, y_i%%ZSMJ28%%, z_i%%ZSMJ29%% (-10^8 \le x_i, y_i, z_i \le 10^8%%ZSMJ30%%), denoting the coordinates of the i%%ZSMJ31%%-th point.
output: Output \frac{n}{2}%%ZSMJ32%% pairs of integers a_i, b_i%%ZSMJ33%% (1 \le a_i, b_i \le n%%ZSMJ34%%), denoting the indices of points removed on snap i%%ZSMJ35%%. Every integer between 1%%ZSMJ36%% and n%%ZSMJ37%%, inclusive, must appear in your output exactly once.
We can show that it is always possible to remove all points. If there are many solutions, output any of them.
note: In the first example, here is what points and their corresponding bounding boxes look like (drawn in two dimensions for simplicity, as all points lie on z = 0%%ZSMJ38%% plane). Note that order of removing matters: for example, points 5%%ZSMJ39%% and 1%%ZSMJ40%% don't form a perfectly balanced pair initially, but they do after point 3%%ZSMJ41%% is removed.
